internal.title: Incident Report: Frontend Service Elevated Error Rate
internal.body:
At 12:34 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered due to a high error rate in the frontend service. Initial diagnosis identified error injection as the primary fault type, supported by a frontend error rate of 0.35 and a checkout service error rate of 0.4. Elevated frontend latency was also noted but considered secondary.

Multiple diagnosis rounds were conducted. Proposed actions to mitigate the issue, including restarting the frontend service, were blocked by guardrails due to missing dry run validation and deployment constraints. Consequently, no direct remediation action was taken during the incident.

The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution. No recovery action was verified during the incident timeframe.

Timeline highlights:
- 12:34 Alert received
- 12:54 Diagnosis round 1: frontend error injection
- 12:54 Proposal refused: no action proposed
- 12:54 Replan due to no action
- 12:54 Diagnosis round 2: frontend error injection
- 12:54 Proposal refused: dry run missing
- 12:55 Replan due to unavailable restart action
- 12:55 Diagnosis round 3: frontend error injection
- 12:55 Proposal refused: no action proposed

Further investigation is ongoing to identify a safe remediation path.

external.title: Service Disruption: Frontend Errors Impacting User Experience
external.body:
Between 12:34 and 12:55 UTC on 2026-11-08, users experienced increased errors when interacting with the frontend service. Our monitoring detected elevated error rates affecting service reliability. We escalated the issue for immediate attention and are actively investigating the root cause.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience as we work to restore full service functionality.
